job.title: Support Worker | Port Stephens Region
job.description:

Our client is a well-established not-for-profit organisation dedicated to enhancing individual wellbeing, empowering people to live independently and creating inclusive communities.

Delivering a diverse range of services across mental health, disability, supported independent living, aged care and community support, the organisation is committed to providing high-quality, person-centred services that make a lasting difference.

With a strong focus on innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement, our client continues to evolve to meet the changing needs of the communities it serves.

We are seeking compassionate and reliable Support Workers to support customers across Port Stephens.

Apply Now

job.title: Aboriginal Community Support Worker | Central Coast
job.description:
athway Talent is proud to partner with a highly respected not-for-profit organisation dedicated to supporting people living with mental health challenges to lead fulfilling, independent, and connected lives.

We are seeking compassionate and motivated Aboriginal Community Support Workers to join a growing Community Living Supports (CLS) team on the Central Coast. Due to continued growth, multiple full-time and part-time opportunities are available within the team.

This is a rewarding opportunity to use your cultural knowledge, community connections, and support experience to empower Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people living with mental health challenges. Working within a recovery-oriented framework, you will help participants increase independence, strengthen community engagement, and achieve their personal wellbeing goals.

About the Role
 As an Aboriginal Community Support Worker, you will provide practical, community-based support to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander participants living with mental health challenges.

Working across the Central Coast region, you will build meaningful relationships with participants, support their recovery and wellbeing goals, strengthen cultural and community connections, and assist them to access services, education, employment, and social opportunities.

You will work collaboratively with participants, families, carers, and key stakeholders to deliver culturally safe, person-centred support that promotes independence, inclusion, and positive outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build positive, professional, and culturally safe relationships with participants.
  • Provide practical support to assist participants in achieving their recovery and wellbeing goals.
  • Facilitate access to community, cultural, recreational, and social inclusion activities.
  • Support participants to attend appointments and connect with relevant services.
  • Assist participants to develop daily living skills and increase independence.
  • Advocate for participant choice, self-determination, and empowerment.
  • Collaborate with families, carers, and service providers to achieve participant outcomes.
  • Maintain accurate case notes, records, and reporting documentation.

Essential Requirements

  • Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander heritage and community connection.
  • Certificate IV in Mental Health, Community Services, Individual Support, Peer Work, or a related qualification (or equivalent industry experience).
  • Minimum 12 months' experience within a Community Living Supports (CLS) program, psychosocial support service, NDIS, mental health, disability, or community services environment.
  • Demonstrated understanding of recovery-oriented and person-centred practice.
  • Knowledge of culturally safe and trauma-informed support approaches.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Sound computer literacy, including Microsoft Office and electronic client management systems.
  • Current NSW Driver's Licence and access to a reliable vehicle.
  • Working With Children Check.
  • National Police Check (issued within the last three months).
  • NDIS Worker Screening Check and NDIS Worker Orientation Module.

What's on Offer?

  • Meaningful work that makes a genuine difference in people's lives.
  • Supportive and inclusive team environment.
  • Ongoing training, development, and professional supervision.
  • Opportunities for career growth within a respected not-for-profit organisation.
  • Salary packaging benefits to maximise your take-home pay.
  • The opportunity to support Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities across the Central Coast.

A Safe and Inclusive Workplace
Pathway Talent and our client have a zero-tolerance approach to abuse, neglect, and harm and are committed to safeguarding the wellbeing of children, young people, people with disability, and the communities we serve.

Successful applicants will be required to undertake relevant pre-employment screening, including a National Criminal History Check and other role-specific compliance checks.

Apply Now
Make a meaningful contribution to the lives of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people across the Central Coast and help support stronger, healthier, and more connected communities.

Pathway Talent acknowledges Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples as the Traditional Custodians of the land and pays respect to Elders past, present, and emerging.

IMPORTANT: This is an identified position under Section 14 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1977 (NSW).

Working closely with senior leadership and cross-functional teams, you will drive product strategy, identify emerging market opportunities, strengthen strategic partnerships and support sustainable organisational growth.

This is a diverse and influential role combining product management, commercial strategy, business development, contract management and tender submissions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Product Strategy & Innovation: Manage the product and service lifecycle, identifying opportunities for improvement, innovation and expansion.
  • Business Growth: Develop and implement strategies to identify new markets, diversify revenue streams and support sustainable organisational growth.
  • Customer-Centred Design: Champion customer insights, market research and co-design methodologies to develop services that respond to changing community needs.

  • Tender & Grant Submissions: Lead and coordinate the development of competitive tenders, funding proposals and grant applications.
  • Commercial & Market Analysis: Conduct market research, financial modelling, cost-benefit analysis and risk assessments to support informed strategic decisions.
  • Stakeholder Collaboration: Work closely with operational leaders, finance, customer experience and other teams to ensure products and services align with organisational objectives.

About You
We are looking for an experienced and forward-thinking Product Manager who brings strong commercial acumen, strategic capability and a passion for delivering meaningful community outcomes.

  • Strong commercial and financial acumen, including financial modelling, analysis and strategic planning.
  • Demonstrated experience in contract management, negotiation and stakeholder engagement.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including the ability to develop tenders, grant applications and strategic submissions.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making capabilities.
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel proficiency.
  • The ability to work autonomously, manage competing priorities and collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders.
  • A genuine commitment to delivering positive social and community outcomes.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
Alongside the opportunity to make a meaningful difference, our client offers a range of benefits designed to support your financial wellbeing, professional development and work-life balance.

  • Generous Salary Packaging: Take advantage of not-for-profit salary packaging benefits of up to $15,900 per year, plus up to $2,650 for eligible meal and entertainment expenses, potentially increasing your take-home pay.
  • Fitness Passport: Access discounted memberships across a wide network of participating gyms, fitness centres and swimming pools to support your health and wellbeing.

  • Purpose-Driven Work: Contribute to services that empower individuals, strengthen communities and create lasting social impact.
  • Strategic Influence: Play an integral role in shaping innovative service offerings, developing partnerships and driving sustainable organisational growth.

Apply Now

job.title: Billings Administrator
job.description:
Pathway Talent is working alongside New Horizons to recruit a Billings Administrator to join its Finance team on a six-month contract, with strong potential to transition to a permanent position.

New Horizons is a not-for-profit organisation with wellbeing at the heart of everything it does. This opportunity will suit someone with billing, claims administration or accounts receivable experience, ideally within the NDIS or community services sector.

About the role
You’ll support accurate and timely NDIS billing, revenue claims and accounts receivable processing, ensuring customer information and financial records are maintained to a high standard.

Working closely with Finance and Service Delivery teams, you’ll process claims, reconcile payments and help resolve rejected claims and outstanding invoices.

What you’ll be doing

  • Process and lodge NDIS payment requests and other revenue claims within required timeframes.
  • Prepare invoices for services, including self-managed participants and customer contributions.
  • Check billing information against customer records and supporting documentation.
  • Investigate rejected and unpaid claims, working with colleagues to resolve discrepancies.
  • Process incoming payments and complete account and bank reconciliations.
  • Issue account statements and follow up outstanding payments.
  • Maintain accurate customer, provider and financial information across relevant systems.
  • Support general accounts receivable duties and improvements to billing processes.

What you’ll bring

  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or significant experience in billing, claims administration or accounts receivable.
  • Strong attention to detail, accurate data entry and sound record keeping.
  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including confidence using Excel to reconcile and analyse information.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate discrepancies.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Clear communication skills and confidence working with different stakeholders.
  • Experience handling sensitive and confidential information.
  • The ability to work independently and collaboratively.

Experience with NDIS billing and claims processing is desirable but not essential.

Experience with CareLink, Microsoft Dynamics NAV or the community services sector will also be well regarded.

Why join?

  • A six-month contract with potential for permanent employment
  • Meaningful work supporting an organisation focused on people and wellbeing.
  • The opportunity to build your experience across NDIS billing, claims and financial operations.
  • Collaboration with Finance and service delivery teams, with scope to contribute ideas and improve processes.

The successful applicant will be required to provide:

  • A satisfactory National Police Check (issued within 3 months)
  • Proof of identity and the right to work in Australia.
  • Evidence of relevant qualifications, where applicable.
  • Current NSW Drivers Licence
  • NDIS worker check (or willingness to obtain)
  • WWCC (or willingness to obtain)

Any additional role-specific screening requirements will be confirmed during the recruitment process.

Our commitment to safety
New Horizons is committed to safeguarding the rights, safety and wellbeing of all customers, including children, young people and adults at risk. We have zero tolerance for abuse, neglect and exploitation and expect all employees to uphold these responsibilities.

Diversity and inclusion
We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected and supported.

job.title: NDIS Billings Coordinator
job.description:
Pathway Talent is partnering with an established and respected not-for-profit organisation to recruit an experienced and detail-oriented NDIS Billing Coordinator.

This is an exciting opportunity to play a vital role in ensuring accurate, timely and compliant NDIS billing, while supporting the delivery of essential services to individuals and communities.

About the Organisation
Our client is a well-established not-for-profit organisation committed to empowering individuals, promoting independence and delivering high-quality, person-centred support.

With a strong presence in the community services sector, the organisation is dedicated to creating positive outcomes for people living with disability and those accessing essential support services.

About the Opportunity
As the NDIS Billing Coordinator, you will take ownership of the end-to-end NDIS billing and claiming process, ensuring services are accurately recorded, invoiced and claimed in accordance with NDIS guidelines.

Working closely with finance, rostering and operational teams, you will play an integral role in maintaining billing accuracy, resolving discrepancies and improving processes to support efficient service delivery.

This is a permanent, full-time opportunity suited to someone who enjoys working with numbers, solving problems and contributing to meaningful community outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

  • NDIS Billing & Claims: Manage the weekly NDIS billing cycle, including bulk uploads and manual claims through PRODA and the relevant NDIS provider portal.
  • Compliance & Accuracy: Ensure claims comply with NDIS Pricing Arrangements, participant funding and service agreements.
  • Data Reconciliation: Reconcile rostering, timesheet and service delivery information against participant budgets and service agreements.
  • Claims Management: Investigate and resolve rejected, adjusted or outstanding claims in a timely manner.
  • Accounts Receivable: Prepare invoices for plan-managed and self-managed participants and follow up outstanding payments.
  • Financial Reconciliation: Reconcile payments, maintain accurate billing records and monitor debtor ageing.
  • Service Agreements: Assist with the preparation and updating of service agreements, quotes and funding documentation.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Respond to billing enquiries from participants, families, plan managers and internal stakeholders.
  • Reporting & Improvement: Monitor billing performance, prepare reports and identify opportunities to streamline processes.

About You
We are looking for a highly organised, analytical and detail-oriented professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment and takes pride in delivering accurate and efficient outcomes.

To be successful, you will bring:

  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrated experience in NDIS billing, accounts receivable or financial administration.
  • Minimum 2 years' experience in NDIS billing, claims processing or a similar finance-related role.
  • Strong understanding of NDIS Pricing Arrangements, claiming requirements and compliance obligations.
  • Experience using PRODA and NDIS claiming systems, including bulk uploads and claims management.
  • Experience with financial, rostering or client management systems, with the ability to learn new platforms quickly.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, lookups and pivot tables.
  • Excellent attention to detail, reconciliation skills and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Confident communication skills and the ability to build positive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • A genuine commitment to supporting positive outcomes for people living with disability.

Essential Requirements
The successful applicant must hold, or be willing and eligible to obtain prior to commencement:

  • NDIS Worker Screening Check.
  • National Police Check.
  • NDIS Worker Orientation Module.
  • Full Australian working rights.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

  • Generous Salary Packaging: Access not-for-profit salary packaging benefits that may increase your take-home pay.
  • Fitness Passport: Enjoy discounted access to participating gyms, fitness centres and swimming pools.
  • Flexible Working Arrangements: Access flexible working options, subject to operational requirements.
  • Additional Leave Options: Access purchased annual leave arrangements.
  • Employee Assistance Program: Confidential counselling and wellbeing support.
  • Professional Development: Opportunities to expand your skills and grow your career.
  • Purpose-Driven Work: Join an organisation dedicated to making a positive difference in the lives of individuals and communities.
  • Collaborative Environment: Work alongside supportive teams committed to delivering quality services.

job.title: Counsellor
job.description:
Pathway Talent is recruiting on behalf of New Horizons Enterprises Ltd for an experienced Carer Counsellor to join the Carer Gateway team.

This role provides an opportunity to support unpaid carers experiencing emotional, psychological and relationship challenges associated with their caring responsibilities. Through short-term therapeutic interventions, you will help carers strengthen their wellbeing, resilience, coping strategies and confidence.

About the Role
 As a Carer Counsellor, you will provide professional, evidence-informed counselling within the Carer Gateway service model.

You will work closely with Carer Navigators, Coaches, multidisciplinary colleagues and external services to ensure carers receive responsive, coordinated and appropriate support. Services may be delivered face-to-face, by telephone and through secure digital platforms.

Your key responsibilities will include:

  • Providing evidence-informed counselling to carers experiencing emotional, psychological and relationship challenges associated with their caring role.
  • Completing psychosocial assessments, formulation and intervention planning.
  • Providing individual, family and group counselling in line with program guidelines.
  • Applying strengths-based, solution-focused, grief and loss, CBT-informed, ACT-informed and trauma-informed approaches where clinically appropriate.
  • Supporting carers to strengthen coping skills, emotional wellbeing, resilience, self-care and confidence.
  • Undertaking risk assessments relating to suicide, self-harm, domestic and family violence, neglect, abuse and other safeguarding concerns.
  • Developing safety plans and escalating identified risks appropriately.
  • Supporting carers to access additional services such as advocacy, aged care, mental health, disability, peer support, coaching and community services.
  • Maintaining accurate and timely clinical records and treatment documentation.
  • Participating in clinical supervision, reflective practice, service development and continuous improvement activities.

About You
 You will bring a professional, compassionate and person-centred approach, together with the clinical capability to support carers experiencing a range of complex circumstances.

To be successful, you will have:

  • A tertiary qualification in Counselling, Psychology, Social Work, Psychotherapy or another relevant behavioural health discipline, with qualifications recognised in Australia.
  • Current accreditation or eligibility for membership with an appropriate Australian professional association, such as the Australian Counselling Association (ACA), Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia (PACFA), or Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW).
  • A minimum of three years’ work experience in Australia.
  • Demonstrated experience delivering therapeutic counselling services, including conducting needs assessments and providing individual counselling sessions.
  • Experience undertaking psychosocial and risk assessments and responding appropriately to identified needs and risks.
  • Demonstrated experience in, and the ability to provide, Rogerian/person-centred and/or Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), or similar therapeutic approaches.
  • Sound knowledge and practical understanding of grief and loss, trauma-informed practice, family systems and strengths-based approaches.
  • A strong understanding of confidentiality, privacy, professional boundaries and ethical practice requirements.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage with clients and build professional, respectful relationships.
  • The ability to work autonomously, manage competing priorities and exercise sound professional judgement, while also working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Strong clinical documentation, record-keeping and computer literacy skills, including the ability to maintain accurate and timely client records.
  • Current professional indemnity insurance appropriate to the relevant professional discipline.

Highly Regarded
It would be advantageous if you also have:

  • Experience supporting carers, families or people affected by disability, mental illness, chronic illness or ageing.
  • Knowledge of Carer Gateway, My Aged Care, disability and community service systems.
  • Experience facilitating therapeutic or psychoeducational groups.
  • An understanding of culturally responsive and trauma-informed practice.
  • Experience working with First Nations communities and culturally diverse populations.

Pre-Employment Requirements
The position description identifies requirements including:

  • National Criminal History Check.
  • Working with Children Check and NDIS Worker Screening Check where required by the contract, duties or service setting.
  • Current unrestricted Australian driver's licence.
  • Access to suitable transport for work-related travel.
  • Evidence of the right to work in Australia.
  • Completion of relevant mandatory and role-specific training.

In line with this commitment, all appointments are subject to the successful completion of relevant pre-employment and safeguarding checks, including background screening, qualification and registration verification, and any role-specific compliance requirements.

We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

job.title: Youth Suicide Prevention Peer Worker
job.description:
Make a meaningful difference

Pathway Talent is recruiting on behalf of a well-established for-purpose organisation with more than 55 years of experience supporting individuals, families and communities. We are seeking a Youth Suicide Prevention Peer Worker to join an innovative psychosocial support program that supports children and young people up to 25 years of age who have lived experience of suicide, suicidality and self-harm.

Grounded in lived experience and peer support, this program provides a safe and supportive environment where young people can connect, build resilience and work towards recovery. We're looking for someone with lived experience who is passionate about walking alongside young people and their support networks, helping them navigate emotional or mental distress and create positive pathways forward.

About the role
Using your own lived experience of recovery, you'll provide tailored, lived experience-driven psychosocial support that meets each young person where they are. Your work will focus on enhancing wellbeing, building resilience and helping young people recover from adversity.

What you'll do

  • Build and maintain strong, trusting relationships with children and young people (CYP), their families and carers, team members and stakeholders.
  • Work collaboratively to assess support needs and deliver supports in line with relevant practice, quality frameworks and standards.
  • Draw on recovery-oriented, trauma-informed and strengths-based practice in all interactions.
  • Co-develop, implement and review realistic, evidence-based support plans with young people, their families and the Clinical Lead.
  • Use your personal lived experience of a suicidal crisis and/or distress to provide peer support meaningfully and purposefully.
  • Participate in intake and review meetings, and contribute to safety planning and risk assessment.
  • Maintain accurate, timely records and support the Clinical Lead with reporting obligations.
  • Contribute to service co-design, Youth Advisory Groups and continuous improvement, working closely with the Lived Experience Lead and other Peer Workers.

What you'll bring

  • Lived experience of ongoing recovery from suicidality, emotional or mental distress, this is essential to the role.
  • Formal peer support training (e.g. Certificate IV in Mental Health or Mental Health Peer Work), or a willingness to undertake it.
  • Experience providing peer-based psychosocial support to children and/or young people in a mental health or similar setting, including contributing to risk assessments and safety plans.
  • Clear, compassionate communication and strong active-listening skills.
  • Proven capacity to apply trauma-informed and recovery-oriented principles with care, respect and a focus on safety.
  • The ability to work within multidisciplinary teams and engage with external stakeholders.
  • Strong organisational and documentation skills.
